subject: Does TMB support CondExp (or something similar)?

messages.author: 402856652ba9dda3
messages.subject: Does TMB support CondExp (or something similar)?
parts: So, the TMB wiki states that one shouldn't condition upon parameters.  This is due to the limitations of the AD engine.  However, CppAD offers CondExp statements to deal with this; hence, I'm wondering if I can use CondExp statements with TMB parameters

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Does TMB support CondExp (or something similar)?
parts: You should only do this if you are sure that your use of CondExp won't lead to a non-differentiable log-likelihood surface ... (i.e., any sharp transitions in likelihood mediated by CondExp statements will cause trouble).

So, the TMB wiki states that one shouldn't condition upon parameters.  This is due to the limitations of the AD engine.  However, CppAD offers CondExp statements to deal with this; hence, I'm wondering if I can use CondExp statements with TMB parameters

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Does TMB support CondExp (or something similar)?
parts: Sometimes the two different branches of the conditional expression are representing the same function, just one is more numerically stable than the other. For example, when the branch represents a pivot in the numerical solution of equations.
